paragraphs: Friend, here's what gets me about Absalom. Nothing he did on that road looked like a crime: a chariot, a handshake, a kiss, a kind word about your case. But the Bible says that in this way he "stole the hearts of the men of Israel" (2 Samuel 15:6). Theft doesn't always kick the door in, and sometimes it walks up smiling and tells you exactly what you want to hear.

Notice what he sold, too. He told people their claims were good and right, but "the king has no deputy to hear you" (2 Samuel 15:3), so he pointed at a gap and made himself the answer. Then he asked to go to Hebron to fulfill a vow to the LORD, and from there he sent spies to say, "Absalom reigns in Hebron!" (2 Samuel 15:7-10). I think the warning is that holy-sounding words and a warm face don't prove a heart is honest.

So how do I bake this into my life? I weigh what people say against the Word, not against how nice they were to me. And I keep my eyes open, because hearts get stolen when nobody is watching. The conspiracy is gaining strength, and this story is FAR from over, friend.
